correctness.rationale: PASS. The sufficiency is exactly Theorem 2.1 of Sangal--Swaminathan for \(lpha, eta\ge0\) and \(\lambda+\mu\ge1\). For \(s=\lambda+\mu<1\), pairing consecutive terms in the even alternating sum is an alternating Riemann-sum identity. Applied to \(u^{1-s}\), it gives the endpoint slope coefficient \(-1/2\); the shifted-coefficient correction is lower order. Applied to \(u^{-s}\sin(yu)\), whose derivative is integrable at zero for \(s<1\), the same pairing gives \(n^sS_n(\pi-y/n)	o-	frac12\sin y\). Thus every fixed \(0<y<\pi\) yields negative even partial sums for large \(n\). These are infinite asymptotic arguments, not finite experiments.
